<!-- section:action -->

1. **Start from the moment you want bread**, then work backwards through the bake, the proof, the shape and the bulk ferment.
2. **Write the evidence that ends each wait** next to its planned time.
3. **Name your fallback**: which step can stretch without harming the loaf. A cold proof usually can; see the [oven module](#/module/hearth-m03).

<!-- section:example -->

### Worked example: a fictional Sunday bake

Bread is wanted at 10:00 on Sunday. Baking takes 45 minutes and the oven needs 45 minutes to heat, so the oven goes on at 08:30. The loaves proof cold from Saturday 16:00, so they are shaped by 15:30 after a bulk ferment that starts at 10:00 once the starter peaks.

<!-- section:template -->

### Your bake plan

| Step            | Planned time | Ends when | Fallback |
| --------------- | ------------ | --------- | -------- |
| Starter feed    |              |           |          |
| Mix             |              |           |          |
| Bulk ferment    |              |           |          |
| Shape and proof |              |           |          |
| Bake            |              |           |          |

<!-- section:limits -->

Times are predictions. Temperature changes every fermentation step, so the evidence column matters more than the time column. The plan does not cover commercial ovens or food-safety rules for selling bread.
